items.text: The GET unsubscribe endpoint will be triggered unintentionally by email client link prefetchers, silently changing users' notification settings

The unsubscribe action requires ensure_logged_in but the unsubscribe URL is embedded in notification emails - when logged-out users click the link, they are silently redirected to the homepage with no error message and no unsubscribe action taken, making the per-topic email unsubscribe feature non-functional for the most common use case
The property name stopNotificiationsText is misspelled in controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 and templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs
Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

unsubscribe returns a 500 error when the logged-in user has no TopicUser row for the topic because TopicUser.find_by returns nil and the next line calls tu.notification_level on it without a nil check
Test for List-Unsubscribe header only checks presence but should assert the value uses the provided unsubscribe_url
logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
Header class has leading dot preventing CSS targeting - Line 10 includes '.previous-discussion' instead of 'previous-discussion' in the class attribute
TopicUser.find_by(...) can return nil if the user has no topic_users row yet, and the subsequent tu.notification_level access will raise, causing 500 errors when hitting the unsubscribe URL
Adding render :show inside perform_show_response renders the template before topics#show sets canonical_url, so every server-rendered topic page loses its <link rel="canonical"> tag
The view exists only to add a CSS class that the template wrapper div could carry directly
About 100 of the 225 changed lines are formatting-only edits unrelated to the feature, obscuring the real change and breaching CONTRIBUTING.md's one-feature-per-branch guidance
Rendering {{title}} inside HTML translation creates an XSS vulnerability on the unsubscribe page because the title is interpolated and inserted with triple-stash without escaping
unsubscribe is behind ensure_logged_in, so a logged-out recipient clicking the email link is redirected to / with no message and no return path; nothing gets unsubscribed
The slug-mismatch redirect uses status: 301 on a URL with side effects; browsers cache it permanently, causing extra redirect hops after slug changes

TopicsController#unsubscribe dereferences the result of TopicUser.find_by(...) without handling the no-row case, which will raise and return a 500 when the current user has no topic_users record for that topic

Template is named for a nested topic.unsubscribe route, but the router/controller/view use the top-level topicUnsubscribe route, so the new page content will not be picked up unless the template is renamed to match that route
TopicUser.find_by can return nil and the next line calls tu.notification_level, causing unsubscribe to return 500 (NoMethodError) for a logged-in user with no topic_users row
The post_number: /\d+/ constraint was quietly dropped from both summary routes and moderator-liked was reordered inside a feature commit
Missing trailing comma in multiline filter list - the array passed to skip_before_filter should include a trailing comma after :unsubscribe to match project style and fix lint warning
The new state-changing endpoint, Topic#unsubscribe_url and the email footer change have no tests, breaching CONTRIBUTING.md 'Include tests' guidance

The unsubscribe route is defined as GET but the controller action mutates TopicUser.notification_level and saves it, making it vulnerable to CSRF via link/image injection since no CSRF token is required on GET requests

TopicsController#unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change() so notifications_reason_id/notifications_changed_at aren't set for a user-initiated notification_level change, allowing update_last_read auto-tracking to later overwrite the user's choice
State-changing unsubscribe action uses GET request - topics#unsubscribe mutates notification state but is mapped to GET, should use POST/PUT or require a signed token
The List-Unsubscribe header still points to user preferences, not the per-topic unsubscribe URL
Typo in stopNotificiationsText property name - should be stopNotificationsText
An in-app Ember transition to topicUnsubscribe only loads topic JSON and never hits the server action, yet still shows the 'stop receiving notifications' confirmation

tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change, so MessageBus notification_level_change publish, notifications_reason_id=:user_changed and notifications_changed_at are all skipped; other open tabs go stale and the old notification reason stays

The unsubscribe_link i18n string now requires %{unsubscribe_url} interpolation but Email::MessageBuilder provides no default value for it - any plugin using build_email with add_unsubscribe_link: true without providing unsubscribe_url will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument

The unsubscribe action steps the notification level down instead of setting a target level, making it non-idempotent - watching/tracking goes to regular on first visit, then to muted on reload/second click, muting topics the user never chose to mute

The shared unsubscribe_link string now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, so any MessageBuilder caller passing add_unsubscribe_link: true without unsubscribe_url hits missing-interpolation handling, and non-English locales keep the old string so they never see the per-topic link
Duplicate respond instructions in email template - Line 6 duplicates the respond instructions that already appear at Line 19 when context_posts are present

The new state-changing behaviour has no tests covering TopicsController#unsubscribe, Topic#unsubscribe_url, the new email footer, the login requirement, the slug redirect, the missing-TopicUser path and the Ember route, breaching CONTRIBUTING.md §3

TopicUser.find_by can return nil and the current toggle logic can re-subscribe users or flip state due to email link prefetching - should make unsubscribe idempotent by always setting to muted and creating the record if needed
The controller exists only to format one i18n string but could be eliminated by using the i18n helper with named params directly in the template
The rewritten tracking scope uses 3-space and 5-space continuation indents, against the file's 2-space convention

topicUnsubscribe is declared as a top-level route, but the template lives at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs (which resolves to topic.unsubscribe), so Ember may not find/render the intended template and the unsubscribe page may render incorrectly or blank
Unsubscribe changes state on a plain GET with no CSRF protection or signed token, allowing any third-party page to change a logged-in victim's notification level for any topic they can see

The unsubscribe endpoint uses plain GET with no CSRF protection and no per-user token, allowing any third-party page to change a logged-in visitor's notification level for any topic (including PMs) via techniques like

The action toggles the level downward instead of setting a target, so it is not idempotent (watching/tracking -> regular, then reload goes regular -> muted), and the confirmation copy is misleading because regular still notifies on replies, mentions and quotes

After a watching/tracking user's first click, the confirmation says 'You will stop receiving notifications' but the server only lowered the level to regular which still notifies on replies, mentions and quotes - the copy promises a state that was not set
The module ends in }) without a semicolon, unlike its sibling .js.es6 controllers

issues.claim: The unsubscribe endpoint is a GET route whose action changes and saves TopicUser.notification_level without CSRF protection or a signed token, so a third-party page (e.g. via ) can change a logged-in user's notification level for any topic they can see.
Because the unsubscribe endpoint is a GET, email client link prefetchers can trigger it and change users' notification settings without the user acting.

The unsubscribe action requires ensure_logged_in, but its URL is sent in notification emails. A logged-out recipient who clicks the link is redirected to / with no message and no return path, and nothing is unsubscribed.
The property name stopNotificiationsText is misspelled; it should be stopNotificationsText.

In TopicsController#unsubscribe, TopicUser.find_by can return nil when the user has no topic_users row for the topic. The next line calls tu.notification_level without a nil check, which raises and returns a 500.

The unsubscribe action steps the notification level down instead of setting a target level, so it is not idempotent. Watching/tracking goes to regular on the first visit and to muted on a reload or prefetch.

After a watching/tracking user's first click, the confirmation says 'You will stop receiving notifications', but the level was only lowered to regular, which still notifies on replies, mentions and quotes.
The test for the List-Unsubscribe header only checks that the header is present, not that its value uses the provided unsubscribe_url.
The List-Unsubscribe header still points to the user preferences page rather than the per-topic unsubscribe URL.
On line 10, the header's class attribute contains '.previous-discussion' with a leading dot, which prevents CSS from targeting it.
Adding render :show inside perform_show_response renders the template before topics#show sets canonical_url, so server-rendered topic pages lose their <link rel="canonical"> tag.
The view exists only to add a CSS class that the template's wrapper div could carry directly.
About 100 of the 225 changed lines are formatting-only edits unrelated to the feature, contrary to CONTRIBUTING.md's one-feature-per-branch guidance.
On the unsubscribe page, {{title}} is interpolated into an HTML translation and inserted with triple-stash without escaping, which allows XSS.
The slug-mismatch redirect for the unsubscribe URL, which has side effects, uses status 301, so browsers cache it permanently.

The template is at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which resolves to a nested topic.unsubscribe route. The router, controller and view use the top-level topicUnsubscribe route, so Ember will not pick up the template.
The post_number: /\d+/ constraint was dropped from both summary routes, and moderator-liked was reordered, inside a feature commit.
The multiline array passed to skip_before_filter has no trailing comma after :unsubscribe.
There are no tests for the new state-changing TopicsController#unsubscribe endpoint, Topic#unsubscribe_url, or the email footer change, contrary to CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Include tests' guidance.

TopicsController#unsubscribe calls tu.save! directly instead of TopicUser.change. As a result, notifications_reason_id/notifications_changed_at are not set and the MessageBus notification_level_change publish is skipped, so update_last_read auto-tracking can later overwrite the user's choice.

The shared unsubscribe_link i18n string now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, but Email::MessageBuilder gives it no default. Any build_email caller passing add_unsubscribe_link: true without unsubscribe_url hits a missing-interpolation error, and non-English locales keep the old string.
An in-app Ember transition to topicUnsubscribe only loads the topic JSON and never calls the server action, yet still shows the 'stop receiving notifications' confirmation.
On line 6, the email template repeats the respond instructions that already appear on line 19 when context_posts are present.
The controller exists only to format one i18n string, which the i18n helper with named params could do directly in the template.
The rewritten tracking scope uses 3-space and 5-space continuation indents, unlike the file's 2-space convention.
The module ends in }) without a semicolon, unlike its sibling .js.es6 controllers.
